title: Is Inner Ear Morphology the Key to the Evolutionary Ecology of Bats?
content: 1.    The exceptional navigational ability of bats relies on specialised sensory organs; specifically, the inner ear is optimised to process high-frequency sounds in total darkness. 2.    Despite its clear functional importance, inner ear morphology remains an underutilised source of evolutionary insight in Chiroptera, particularly the origins of echolocation and deep-time phylogenetic divergences. 3.    Here, we review specialised anatomy of the chiropteran inner ear and contrast bat inner ear ecology with recent insights from echolocating whales 4.    We address methodological challenges of studying minute features, demonstrate how non-destructive digital imagery advances overcome traditional barriers, and consider how confounding effects of phylogeny could be addressed in quantitative analyses.  5.    We argue that known strong correlations between echolocation strategy and flight space point to excellent opportunities to use chiropteran inner ear morphology to infer the origins and evolution of chiropteran ecology and echolocation behaviour.
